question: What was the name of the new department opened by Muhammad Tughlaq for the development of agriculture?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Diwan-i-Kohi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Diwan-i-Kohi** was established by Muhammad bin Tughlaq to promote agricultural development in his kingdom.
 
• This department was tasked with improving **irrigation facilities** and reclaiming uncultivable land to increase agricultural productivity.
 
• Muhammad Tughlaq allocated funds from the royal treasury to assist farmers with seeds, tools, and other agricultural necessities.
 
• The initiative aimed to ensure food security and strengthen the economy by boosting agricultural output during his reign.
 
• This department reflects Muhammad bin Tughlaq's interest in administrative reforms and innovative measures, though many of his policies faced challenges in implementation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Muhammad bin Tughlaq:** The Sultan of Delhi from 1325 to 1351, known for his ambitious and controversial policies.
 
• **Innovative Policies:** Muhammad Tughlaq introduced several reforms, including the shifting of the capital to Daulatabad and the introduction of token currency.
 
• **Challenges:** Many of his initiatives failed due to poor execution, lack of planning, and resistance from the populace.
 
• **Diwan-i-Kohi:** A significant attempt to enhance agricultural productivity, although its success was limited due to administrative inefficiencies and climatic factors.
 
• **Legacy:** Despite his failures, Muhammad bin Tughlaq is remembered as a ruler with visionary ideas and a focus on economic and administrative reforms.
